speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We cannot allow disappointment of laid off workers to turn to despair.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We cannot stand for vulnerable groups in our society to be devoid of hope.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: We cannot kick the can down the road for our children to tackle climate change.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Hence, we should tackle it now for them.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: I am glad that this is the spirit of Deputy Prime Minister Heng Swee Keat’s Budget Statement and it has underscored the actions that will be taken right here, right now.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: The theme of this Budget 2021 "Emerging Stronger Together" resonates with me.

speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim (Chua Chu Kang)
text: Because if we persevere, stay the course and navigate through the storm, then we will be the ones making the waves in this ocean.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, I must thank the Leader of the House for giving me this unenviable task.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I believe this year’s Budget is a continuation of that spirit, that is, timely aid to citizens and companies in need.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I believe that COVID-19 has shown the world the best of Singapore and how we have stood together to overcome.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It is with this spirit – of a common humanity and our common identity as Singaporeans – that I wish to speak today.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: My first point is how we should strive towards becoming one united Singaporean family.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Multi-culturalism is a significant ingredient in our Singapore tapestry.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In fact, as we continue to embrace multi-culturalism and diversity, and the more we understand the differences and the richness of each culture, the tighter our social fabric becomes.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: We do value the diversity in our ethnic heritages.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It shows that we value the different cultures inherent in our society and aid each subsequent generation to become familiar with the traditions and outlook of each ethnic group.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: These self-help groups help their individual communities while also carrying out joint inter-racial events.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This helps foster both the bonds within each individual community and also the bonds in the larger Singaporean context.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I support this as it is in line with the spirit of enhancing ties between people of various ethnic backgrounds who become neighbours and who then share common environments.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I believe that as we continue to strengthen and understand different ethnic communities, and as our diverse culture and heritage become more and more a part of Singapore, race will become less and less a factor in evaluating a person.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In fact, I would dare say that race matters less in the minds of Singaporeans, especially those who are younger, in comparison to their nationality, than that of being Singaporean.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Instead of being evaluated based on race, we can evaluate based on more robust factors, such as the person’s character, abilities, values and experience.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In my personal view, ceteris paribus, when it comes to leading the Government, I think it should be the best man for the job, regardless of race.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, if there is a Singaporean Chinese candidate of the right age and with the right character and the right skillset making him the best man for the job, he should be chosen for the job.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: If there is a Singaporean of a minority race of the right age and with the right character and right skillset to be the best man for the job, I think he should be chosen for the job.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Leadership within the Government comes with years of experience and years of being an elected Member within this House.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It could easily be 20 years before an elected Member becomes a Prime Minister and, by that time, the familiarity and connection that people would have with the Minister would count for more than just his race.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: COVID-19 has shown, more than ever, the need for good government and good leadership of and in government.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I know many people my age and younger do want the best man to lead the Government, regardless of race.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Some may say I am being overly idealistic, to the discount of pragmatism.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Because the very idea of a multiracial, multicultural Singapore was an ideal, an aspiration, born, literally, from the tears and the sweat of our founding fathers.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And inch by inch, year by year, we grow closer to making it a reality.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: We are too small a nation to discount a man based on his race.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This is my view, based on my personal belief.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I am not saying race is not important.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Neither am I saying race should be used to dichotomise and polarise.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I am firmly of the view that multi-racial Singapore is important and we should not dilute the significance of race and what it can bring to the table.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: In fact, it brings such a rich tapestry such that many parts of the world can see themselves in us, in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: But when it comes to leadership of government, we should not discount anybody because of their race, but instead evaluate the candidate based on who is best for the job.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I know many in my age group and younger hold this belief firmly too.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Maybe this will happen in 15 to 20 years' time when the party holding the majority of the House chooses the 5G or 6G Prime Minister of who the 5G or 6G Prime Minister should be.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: However, it being 20 years away should not deter us from having such conversations now.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: I do not want any room for my speech to be misinterpreted.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, let me say categorically that I do believe that our Prime Minister is the best man for the job.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And I also do believe that the 4G Ministers have chosen the best man for the job to eventually lead their team.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, nothing in my speech should distract from those conclusions.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Look at Angela Merkel – a woman leading a solid government.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: If we were to straightjacket our perception of talent, we could very well lose out on the best person for the job.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Being a Singaporean is the key identity marker in Singaporeans of my age group and younger.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The second identity marker – that of race – comes after the first identity marker – which is, being Singaporean.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It comes from deep within and I would like to share a story that speaks to the heart of these beliefs of mine.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: My wife and I have four children aged between one and 12 years old.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Her ethnic lineage is pure Chinese and we adopted her at birth in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: What happened was that there was a young Singaporean Chinese woman who found out she was pregnant.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: She decided to carry on with her pregnancy, delivered the baby and put the baby up for adoption.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: She got in touch with a Christian charity who helped place babies with adoptive families.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: My wife and I had put our names down with the charity as potential adoptive parents.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: My wife and I prayed about it and took the leap of faith in adopting this little Singaporean Chinese baby girl.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Today, my daughter is completely part of our family.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: She is the younger sister to our first daughter and dotes on her two younger siblings.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: All our children are loved and treated equally, and are being brought up first and foremost as Singaporeans first; and secondly, as Singaporean Eurasians.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: If it is merely defined by virtue of blood lineage, our second daughter would be Chinese.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: But if it was also defined by culture, then living experience would play a part too.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: My second daughter put up the Chinese New Year decorations made up of hongbaos around our house this year.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: But during the Christmas season, she would eat all the Eurasian fare on the dining table, including sugee cake and even ask for seconds.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: To pre-empt her wondering why she looked a little different from her older sister, my wife and I told her when she was very young, "You came from your tummy mummy; but you were born in our hearts." It is the same way I view Singapore – we are all given life from our mother's wombs but we are all born with Singapore in our hearts.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, when I say being Singaporean is the pre-eminent identity marker of a citizen and that race is a secondary identity marker, I believe that firmly.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: There is no binary lens with which one should view race such that race completely does not matter or always matters to the discount of everything else.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It is a spectrum – a spectrum that is a continuum within which my daughter, of Singaporean Chinese lineage and living in a Singaporean Eurasian home, is completely comfortable.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Race is an asset to make the tapestry of Singapore culture richer and our identity fuller.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: So, let it not divide us but unite us in always choosing the right person to lead our Government.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The next point I want to make relates to adoption, a point which I have shared, I care deeply about.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: As I have said, the pandemic has shown the strength and depth of our community bonds, as people reached out to those around them and blessed their neighbours and helped the vulnerable.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: But there is a particular group of vulnerable people who are not afforded the same protection that other citizens have.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: These are the stateless people living in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: They do not vote but they, too, need a voice in Parliament.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Many have grown up in Singapore and many were even born in Singapore.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: They live here, work here and have families here.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Yet, because their parents failed to register their birth at the time of their birth, some are denied citizenship and live their lives as stateless people.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This impacts them in their daily life as some struggle to open bank accounts, buy or rent houses and even find a job.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Such difficulties present a very real challenge for them.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: It leaves them in the lurch and vulnerable.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: This pandemic has brought the best out of Singapore.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: The pandemic has not deterred Singapore's determination to build a better future for our children.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: Olive trees still grow on the equator at Gardens by the Bay.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And we are not done turning a mudflat into a thriving metropolis.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And inch by inch, yard by yard, we strive in this House – and out there in the streets – to become a more united country, regardless of race.

speaker: Mr Christopher de Souza (Holland-Bukit Timah)
text: And that is a future worth fighting for.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Normally, the Round-up speech is shorter than the Budget speech but this year, it may be different.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I also want to thank Mr Christopher de Souza for his very moving and personal speech of what it means to be a Singaporean.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And also let me thank Mr Liang Eng Hwa, Chairman of the Government Parliamentary Committee (GPC) for Finance and Trade and Industry, for laying out the big picture and key issues clearly.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Liang spoke about supporting our people through the immediate pain of the crisis and the need to take action to emerge stronger.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Importantly, he did not shy away from the difficult conversation of how these important measures need to be funded and offered constructive suggestions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This sets the stage for this House to discuss the way forward.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I also thank Ms Foo Mee Har who not only spoke passionately about supporting our people and businesses, but also suggested how to do so in a prudent and sustainable manner.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over the last few days, the passionate debate went along a few threads.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some Members elevated the debate to help Singaporeans appreciate the changing landscape and the need to act.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some Members highlighted the importance of our reserves, the bold and decisive response mounted and what it achieved.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Unfortunately, some argued selectively without acknowledging the broader impact of COVID-19 and the outcomes of the Government's decisive interventions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Before I dive into the issues raised by Members, I want to situate Budget 2021 and Singapore's future within the larger forces sweeping the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singapore sits at the crossroads between the East and the West.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is a position that we have harnessed to maintain our relevance to the world amid the flux and changing tides of global political and economic developments.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But we cannot take our standing in the world for granted.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is something that we have to painstakingly maintain, as the world and region evolve, so that we remain relevant.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For some time, we have observed the gradual geopolitical and technological shifts.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The world was slowly adapting to a rising China, which found its place alongside the US as an economic and military powerhouse.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Fortunately, the deep interdependence of markets and supply chains served as a stabiliser for world order, as well as international trade and commerce.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But COVID-19 disrupted this tenuous equilibrium and accelerated bifurcation and change.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Overnight, this virus revealed the vulnerabilities of inter-connected supply chains.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The race for vaccines and the rush for economic recovery have also surfaced nationalist tendencies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These events will play a significant part in countries' and businesses' calculations, as they rebuild their value chains and business networks.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Countries will seek for greater onshoring of their key industries for resilience.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Businesses may re-think their globalisation strategy and approach, giving more weight to resilience and reliability.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singapore can capitalise on them to emerge stronger, become more competitive and remain relevant to the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, nations and businesses will place a high premium on partners and locations which are reliable and predictable in their dealings.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is where we can leverage the strong Singapore brand, globally trusted for long-term planning, openness and reliability.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, as the flow of people pulled back because of the lockdowns, the flow of digital information and knowledge spiked.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There is potential for Singapore to ride on the rise of technology adoption and digital economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Third, climate change is a threat for humanity.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must do our part, create new opportunities from the global interest in sustainable development.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: My Budget Statement laid out our strategic plan to capitalise on our strengths and to double down on our commitment to invest in connectivity, digitalisation, the green economy, and of course, our people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, I will round up this Budget Debate by speaking on Members' contributions along three themes: our economic strategy to emerge stronger; a cohesive and liveable Singapore and a prudent fiscal strategy for the long term.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Since then, I have heard many views on the appropriateness and adequacy of our economic response.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some have called for more support, while others have asked if we are doing too much.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: COVID-19 has caused the worst global economic crisis since the Great Depression.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is equivalent to 255 million full-time jobs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Economists also warn of possible scarring, with long-term GDP losses, rising public and corporate debt, higher hurdles on capital spending, and continued rise in unemployment levels.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We disbursed a total of $27.4 billion in grants to provide relief, preserve jobs and help firms build capabilities to pivot to new growth areas – more than 18 times the amount disbursed in 2019.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As many Members including Mr Liang Eng Hwa and Mr Desmond Choo thoughtfully reminded us, we narrowly averted a much deeper recession and scarring.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: More details of our early findings can be found in the interim assessment of the COVID-19 measures that MOF released earlier this year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The impulses from last year's measures continue to flow through the economy to complement Budget 2021.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The combined effects of the two years' Budgets imply a material support to GDP in 2021.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our calibrated strategy to support businesses and protect livelihoods has seen positive outcomes for firms and workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We tilted support towards the hardest-hit sectors to help them retain core capabilities and prepare for recovery.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, some of these sectors are starting to see light at the end of the tunnel.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, with the phased resumption of activities domestically since June 2020, the consumer-facing sectors, including retail and food services, saw a gradual recovery to around 85% of pre-COVID-19 output levels by Q4 in 2020.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many firms have made good use of the support we rolled out.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Almost all recipients were micro, small and medium-sized enterprises, or SMEs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Enterprise Singapore also supported more than 15,000 companies in raising productivity, going international and undertaking innovation projects.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, I am glad businesses were taking innovation more seriously during this COVID-19 period.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: When COVID-19 struck, the yoga studio halted on-site classes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: After consulting an SME Centre, Mindful Movement tapped on the Productivity Solutions Grant to transit their classes online.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, they continue to offer both online and physical classes, to provide clients greater choice and flexibility.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For sectors that remain badly affected, I will continue to provide targeted relief and support to help them transform and reposition themselves for recovery.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: On the workers front, the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package has helped to cushion the labour market fall-out and preserve the livelihoods of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many jobseekers joined industries with a promising growth outlook through the Jobs Growth Incentive, or JGI, and drew the same or higher wages.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Ministry of Manpower will provide more details at the COS.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Close to 80% of them were placed into jobs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Of these job placements, six in 10 were long-term jobs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Growth sectors such as InfoComm Technology or ICT, healthcare, and manufacturing, accounted for most of the placements.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We tilted support towards mature jobseekers, recognising the higher hurdles they faced with career transitions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Based on preliminary estimates, mature workers aged 40 and above accounted for about half of the first 110,000 JGI beneficiaries, and about half of the 76,000 locals placed in SGUnited jobs and skills opportunities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This includes more than 8,000 mature jobseekers placed last year on career conversion programmes, like the TechSkills Accelerator and Professional Conversion Programmes, or PCPs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These schemes enable trainees to reskill for jobs with good growth prospects.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, about seven in 10 PCP participants earn higher wages after starting their new jobs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Goh Che Yong has been in tourism for close to 24 years, dealing in traditional sales for walk-in customers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: He witnessed the digital disruption to the industry.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At 55 years-young, Che Yong embarked on the Professional Conversion Programme for Digital Sales Executive with Siam Express last March.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Although he was still in the same travel industry, moving from traditional to digital sales was not easy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But with the structured training, he gained confidence.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Che Yong now applies his newly acquired digital skills in his job and enjoys exploring new ways of packaging holidays for a post-COVID world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We averted a "COVID generation" of workers and students by preserving human capital and enhancing their employability.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Compared to the 2019 cohort, although full-time permanent employment fell by about 10 percentage points, overall employment rates for this year's fresh IHL graduates remained similar to past years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In particular, 94% of autonomous university graduates in 2020 found employment or got into a traineeship within six months, compared to 91% in 2019.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The SGUnited Traineeships programme has contributed significantly to this outcome.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It has placed close to 5,400 recent graduates into traineeships, to help them gain useful skills and industry experience, and prepare them for the recovery.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Chen Jiahao embarked on a traineeship last year with Taiger Singapore, an Artificial Intelligence, or AI start-up.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Although he had no prior experience in AI or data science, the traineeship enabled Jiahao to pursue his dream of working in deep tech.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: He picked up new skills quickly and developed a Natural Language Processing model to perform information extraction.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Taiger was impressed by Jiahao's strong performance and hired him as a full-time Junior Software Engineer within six months of the start of his traineeship.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In this Budget, I also extended the JGI to September 2021.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I hope this encourages more employers to convert trainees to employees in a timely manner.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Overall, we have managed to mitigate the impact of COVID-19 on our young.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Looking back, the waters of 2020 have been rough.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But we have kept our ship intact, with all hands on deck pulling together to navigate it out of the storm.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In 2021, our suite of support measures, including the further extension to the JSS, the SGUnited Jobs and Skills Package, and targeted support for the worst-hit sectors, will continue to provide a stabilising effect on our economy, amid uncertainties and risks in the global economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Domestically, the pace of border re-opening has slowed amid the global surge in COVID-19 cases and the emergence of new virus strains.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Nevertheless, the COVID-19 situation within Singapore remains under control.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Against this backdrop, the Singapore economic recovery over the course of the year is expected to be gradual and uneven across sectors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Outward-oriented sectors are expected to benefit from the pick-up in external demand, while domestic industries improve as activities safely resume.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Now is the time to chart our course, position ourselves to catch the winds of opportunity and sail boldly in a reshaped world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: That is the focus of this year’s Emerging Stronger Together Budget.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The COVID-19 Resilience Package continues to provide near-term support to safeguard lives, jobs, supply chains, and core capabilities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At the same time, we are also dedicating substantial fiscal resources towards raising the productive capacity of the economy in the medium to long term.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I also applaud our Labour Movement, led by Secretary-General Mr Ng Chee Meng, for their excellent contributions to this debate.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, as Deputy Secretary-General Mr Heng Chee How mentioned, the way forward is as much about being Stronger Together, as it is about Emerging Stronger.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A number of our businesses and workers will hold their own against the best in the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But at the end of the day, we compete as one Team Singapore, not worker by worker, or enterprise by enterprise.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is the strength of our collective capabilities and connectedness, as an economy and as a society, that will determine how far we will go.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, several Members, including Deputy Secretary-General Dr Koh Poh Koon, highlighted the synergies between firms and workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The fortunes of businesses and workers are inextricably linked, more so today than ever.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Demand shocks caused by COVID-19 have exacerbated labour market dislocations and skills mismatches.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Coupled with the structural shift of shorter technology cycles, it will be increasingly difficult for firms to find candidates with the perfect skill sets.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, I urge businesses to look beyond hiring just "plug-and-play" workers, and see the potential within jobseekers to learn and grow in your firms.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am glad to see our local banking community leading the way in grooming new fintech talent like Ms Choo Cui Ling through career conversion.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: After working in IT audit, Cui Ling enrolled in the Technology in Finance Immersion Programme with OCBC Bank.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A few months into her attachment, she was converted into a full-time employee.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: She now helps to coordinate information risk management for the bank in her role as Assistant Manager.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At the same time, jobseekers should keep an open mind, be receptive to new and different job roles, and take the initiative to build new skills.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Third, I am heartened by the Labour Movement’s forward-looking approach on bringing firms and workers together to ride the waves of change and emerge stronger.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Technological advancements promise new possibilities as well as challenges.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As Mr Melvin Yong starkly put, "every job is at risk". "Working from home" will also mean "Working from anywhere" – so job competition can come from any corner of the globe with an internet link.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For our businesses, while e-commerce opens them to a global pool of customers, it also opens their customers to the global pool of sellers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This seeks to give our workers and businesses a distinct advantage in the global marketplace.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Another $19.6 billion of fresh funding will go toward new digitalisation measures and enhanced enterprise development support, as well as worker support measures such as the extension of the SGUnited Jobs and Skills package to support jobseekers in upskilling and accessing employment opportunities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Together, these measures seek to stimulate private investment over a longer horizon and boost the supply-side capacity of the post-COVID economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will help Singapore capitalise on the post-COVID economic recovery and emerge stronger.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This Emerging-Stronger component of the Budget therefore has a strong medium-term orientation through an enduring effect on supporting the level of labour productivity in the economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Members including Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim spoke about what the post-COVID-19 world means for Singapore’s economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To pave the way for our next lap of growth, we must make the following moves.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, we must remake Singapore as a Global-Asia node of technology, innovation and enterprise.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This requires enhancing our connectivity, including digital connectivity, and positioning our firms and workers at the intersection of key global chains growing out of Asia and ASEAN nations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, as Mr Gan Thiam Poh highlighted, we must shift to a technologically advanced, innovation-driven economy, where firms and workers are equipped with the skills to harness technology and intangible assets as a key differentiator.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Third, we must invest in economic resilience and sustainability as a source of competitive advantage.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Building on previous Budgets, Budget 2021 invests in our economic toolkit to support these moves – or as Mr Shawn Huang aptly summarised, to "survive, pivot and develop an edge to seize opportunities of the future".

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: If we get this right, we can set our economy on a path of growth for the next five to 10 years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Building a stronger Singapore Core is at the heart of our approach, as several Members including Ms Jessica Tan and Mr Abdul Samad rightly noted.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The ultimate goal of economic growth is to improve the jobs and lives of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The only way to sustain such improvements is by raising productivity, where firms transform in ways that bring workers along.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Dr Tan Wu Meng spoke about our $19 billion Research, Innovation and Enterprise 2020, or RIE 2020 plan, and its potential returns on investment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: RIE is a cornerstone of Singapore’s efforts to develop as an innovation-led economy and society with good jobs for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The payoffs from investments in research take time to manifest.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have nevertheless made good progress and the results are promising.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: One example is in the biomedical sciences, where Singapore’s RIE investments since 2000 have helped set the foundation for the flourishing sector it is today.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, the biomedical sector makes up almost 4% of GDP, and four of the world’s top 10 drugs by global revenue are made in Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have also established capabilities to develop innovative solutions to national challenges, including in managing the pandemic.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our researchers have worked with local companies to develop and manufacture diagnostic test kits, such as the Fortitude 2.0 test kit, that are now used both locally and in more than 45 countries worldwide.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: All of these would not have been possible without our sustained investments to build up our RIE capabilities over many years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Members including Ms Poh Li San have underscored the importance of supporting businesses to emerge stronger.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The uneven impact of COVID-19 across industries and enterprises means that each enterprise segment requires different support to recover, grow and thrive.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I agree with Mr Edward Chia on the need to adopt a differentiated, life-cycle approach to enterprise development.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our agencies offer a holistic suite of support schemes targeted at the needs of each enterprise segment, by sector and growth stage.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And we approach it not just at the company-level, but at the industry-level, to achieve value-chain transformation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I spoke about the Built Environment sector coming together to transform decisively across developers, consultants, contractors and suppliers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will build on our Alliances for Action to enable more industries to transform together.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will continue to invest in future engines of growth to create new opportunities for our firms and workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Dr Lim Wee Kiak and Miss Cheryl Chan spoke about the importance of nurturing and harnessing the growth of the green economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The green economy is a key part of the future economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Making bold investments now will give us a head-start and create many good jobs for Singaporeans in future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will work with businesses to meet the rising demand for more sustainable products and services.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We committed resources to sustainability efforts under our Research, Innovation and Enterprise or RIE 2020, and will allocate even more for this in the next five years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Helping local SMEs expand their potential remains a focus.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Most of our workers are employed in SMEs, so the success of SMEs will enable our workers to have better jobs and better pay.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Budget 2021 builds on a large existing base of measures, to provide significant enhanced support for SMEs to digitalise, innovate, and transform to seize new opportunities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, to encourage more local SMEs to embark on transformation efforts and venture abroad, I extended the support levels of the Productivity Solutions Grant, the Enterprise Development Grant and the Market Readiness Assistance grant until March 2022.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And as several Members of Parliament and Mr Mark Chay observed, the pandemic has forced many to take an extraordinary digital leap.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To help firms confidently take this leap forward, we have also introduced a suite of digitalisation support, including the Chief Technology Officer-as-a-Service initiative and the Digital Leaders Programme.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Ministry of Communications and Information will announce more details at the COS.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have also provided substantial support to SMEs through last year’s Budgets.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As I mentioned earlier, we take an eco-system approach to economic development, to support workers and companies across all sectors to reach their full potential.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Leon Perera pointed to the synergy of having MNCs and SMEs work together – let me add that this synergy is not just between MNCs and SMEs, but across all companies and sectors – from Large Local Enterprises to SMEs, and even among SMEs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our economic agencies actively support companies in their efforts to transfer capabilities to upskill our local workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This includes the PACT scheme to support knowledge transfer and co-innovation activities between large enterprises and their local suppliers, and initiatives on knowledge transfer and skills training, such as the SkillsFuture Leadership Development Initiative.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Ministry of Trade and Industry will elaborate on this at the COS.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have covered how we will sustain a virtuous eco-system of innovative and competitive firms that support a vibrant economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: All of these efforts serve to create opportunities for our people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To help workers capture these opportunities and enjoy the fruits of growth, we have moved into helping workers get into growth areas, and equipping them with skills to secure sustainable livelihoods.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our immediate priority is to build upon the skills and experience that workers have accumulated, while breaking down barriers so that they can access new jobs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As Mr Abdul Samad put it, not just to equip workers with skills today, but also to prepare them for jobs of tomorrow.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Sam Ong was amongst the 7,200 jobseekers who enrolled in the SGUnited Skills programme last year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: He was retrenched from an offshore construction company in the oil and gas industry due to the impact of COVID-19 and the industry downturn.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Sam recognised the importance of digital skills amid the future job market and enrolled in the Building and Construction Authority’s SGUnited Skills Diploma in Integrated Digital Delivery.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: He found the course useful and looks forward to securing a role in a company that would allow him to apply his new skills.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To equip workers with industry-relevant skills, we are partnering market leaders to conduct quality training at scale.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, Google, Boston Consulting Group and Siemens are partnering SkillsFuture Singapore to offer SGUnited Mid-Career Pathways programmes in ICT, professional services and advanced manufacturing.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These help local jobseekers adapt to the changing technology trends in a shifting labour market.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am confident that these efforts will put our workers in a stronger position to seize new opportunities in the recovering economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Patrick Tay has highlighted employability and job security as top concerns of workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These are important and closely interlinked focus areas in our medium-term jobs and skills strategy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The employment landscape is evolving rapidly, with technology being a key driver and enabler.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some jobs are becoming redundant, while new ones are created.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Hence, job security is fundamentally about staying employable, rather than staying employed in the same job.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will thus continue to strengthen the skills eco-system, which comprises workers, businesses, unions and trade associations and chambers or TACs, through SkillsFuture.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am heartened to see more Singaporeans making good use of our support to take ownership of learning and acquire skills, even in the midst of the pandemic.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: After a 23-year-long career in architecture and project management, he switched to the healthcare sector, so as to better care for his ageing parents.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: He became a freelance home care-giver last year to provide home-based care-giving for seniors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: When the SGUnited Skills programme was launched, Melvin decided to enrol in the Therapy Assistant course at HMI Institute.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Using his SkillsFuture Credits, he was fully covered for the subsidised course fee of $500.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Melvin is keen to continue his journey in the healthcare industry as a Therapy Assistant when he completes the course this year and I wish him all the best!

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, businesses playing their part, to enable workers to build skills.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our firms have come onboard to make workplace learning a priority.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Since 2018, the National Centre of Excellence for Workplace Learning has helped about 180 enterprises per year implement or enhance workplace learning processes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Last year, 3,400 enterprises sent their employees for training in courses supported under the SkillsFuture Enterprise Credit, and about 250 enterprises benefited from partnerships with SkillsFuture anchor companies to enhance their employee skills development and workplace learning capabilities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Deputy Secretary-General Dr Koh Poh Koon highlighted that upskilling and job redesign must come together for pervasive transformation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: By redesigning jobs and training workers to take up the new jobs, employers not only help workers stay employed, but also enable the firms to thrive.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will continue to provide strong support to companies on this front.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This includes operation and technology roadmapping, or OTR, that integrates upskilling to achieve a long-term growth strategy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Environmental services company SembWaste, in partnership with the Building Construction and Timber Industries Employees' Union and the NTUC Training and Transformation, formed the Company Training Committee and embarked on an OTR process to develop a five-year business growth strategy to support Singapore's green targets.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And to support these transformation plans, SembWaste is upskilling its workers in areas such as digital technology.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It has also adopted the Progressive Wage Model to ensure sustainable wage increases tied to skills and productivity growth.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Third, our unions and TACs can reach out to more firms and promote deeper collaboration between firms and workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, the Singapore Business Federation, or SBF, in partnership with Workforce Singapore, leads the Industry 4.0 Human Capital Initiative, to help companies adopt Industry 4.0 through job redesign.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I also thank the Labour Movement for their tireless efforts in supporting the lifelong employability of workers, across different segments with different needs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: NTUC Job Security Council and Company Training Committees are an important innovation for NTUC to partner companies and the Government, to achieve synergy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Ms Janet Ang and Mr Patrick Tay have spoken about the importance of ensuring fair access to employment opportunities for Singaporeans, while remaining open to global talent to complement local capabilities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: MOM will elaborate on this at the COS.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As Mr Henry Kwek mentioned, our TACs can support firms and workers to emerge stronger, by helping them to transform in a pervasive and sustained way.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over the past year, I am encouraged to see TACs rallying the business community together to fight the crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over 2,700 businesses are expected to benefit from these initiatives.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This includes the $1 million Singapore Contractors Association Limited, or SCAL COVID-19 Fund, set up to help construction sector firms cope with the increased operational requirements due to COVID-19.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some 500 member SMEs will stand to benefit from this Fund.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Apart from STEER, the Fund also received contributions from BCA, over 50 SCAL members and the SBF Foundation Compassion Fund that Ms Janet Ang spoke about in her speech.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Singapore Malay Chamber of Commerce and Industry, or SMCCI, also formed a COVID-19 taskforce in March last year, to support members affected by the crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It set up an emergency hotline, organised individual outreach sessions to about 400 members, provided legal advice to those in need, and connected businesses to available Government support measures.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: SMCCI also showcased members who transformed their businesses in the wake of COVID-19 on their specially curated platform, "Discussions @ Dewan", so that others can learn from their successes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The SBF has also been working closely with the National Jobs Council and 31 TACs, to conduct job matching on a business-to-business level, both within and across sectors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Since the start of the pandemic, SBF has assisted more than 600 companies and more than 100 workers have been successfully matched to 77 companies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Through these collaborations, our firms and workers can emerge stronger in a post-COVID world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And as you can see, this is a case where really everyone is putting in their effort and working together.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Members like Mr Lim Biow Chuan spoke about how Singapore has come out relatively unscathed from COVID-19, and how we are starting from solid ground.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Looking around the world, beyond the economic impact, we also see broader health and social impacts.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: One year on, some countries have not recovered from the initial wave of the outbreak.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many are still seeing new COVID-19 cases in the thousands each day, and repeated cycles of lockdowns.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This has wrought havoc on their communities, disrupting livelihoods and day-to-day activities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: People are putting the future on hold to focus on surviving the crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In December 2020, UNESCO reported that, globally, classrooms for nearly one in five school children were closed.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In some countries, healthcare services are still overwhelmed by COVID-19 cases, leaving little help for those with other needs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In Singapore, many of us have resumed our daily activities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Jobs and opportunities to learn new skills remain available.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our young children are back in schools physically and equipped with digital devices for learning.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are looking forward to the future and are working towards our dreams.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As we heard from Mr Lim Biow Chuan earlier, people are still looking to buy cars "as if there was no recession at all"!

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: While we should count our blessings, let us not forget that we are still in the eye of a raging global storm – there are still challenges ahead and there are still individuals and families who are under stress.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Budget 2021 focuses our efforts and resources on emerging stronger.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have shared how we are taking a long-term view and working to support transformation of our economy and workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But I want to assure Members that the Government has also been putting in place multiple layers of support, which will continue to provide targeted, customised relief to help Singaporeans differently affected by COVID-19 and the uneven, K-shaped recovery.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, we have broad-based, permanent schemes to provide strong social support and safety nets that protects all Singaporeans, especially the vulnerable.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We cushioned the vulnerable against the worst of the crisis and mitigated social inequality.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Pritam Singh pointed out the divergence between the data on inequality, and the lived experience on the ground.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are fully aware that there are families who have been deeply impacted by the pandemic, and some more than others.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is exactly why we have tilted our support significantly towards the lower income and vulnerable groups, and Government has partnered the community to reach out to those groups during this period.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Singh himself noted that there was and I quote, "not-insignificant" support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, you have to see the support in totality – the full set of support – and not conclude from one sample because these are rigorous study of what his happening throughout Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Members, including Mr Patrick Tay, Prof Hoon Hian Teck and Mr Louis Chua suggested that we study the viability of an unemployment insurance for workers affected by involuntary employment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the midst of significant disruption, interim, bridging support is needed to tide workers over.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Longer term, while an unemployment insurance appears attractive, this would not be sustainable without longer-term structures to help our workers bounce back.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This sentiment is echoed in other countries like Germany, Sweden and South Korea, where unemployment insurance schemes are linked to active labour market policy measures which seek to get the affected worker back into a job quickly and avoid skills atrophy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: An unemployment insurance would also have its complexities, as Prof Hoon and Mr Tay have pointed out.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Instead, as Mr Xie Yao Quan said, a job is the best welfare.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is more sustainable to ensure that workers maintain a source of income, and to up-skill and re-skill our workers so that they can bounce back quickly from job disruptions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But at the same time, I recognise that as the global economy goes through an even faster pace of change, the nature of jobs and skills will be changing faster too.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will partner our business leaders, Labour Movement and academics to study how to support employability and help those who falter, through measures that suit our context.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Mr Gerald Giam claimed that our middle income receive little support for their cost of living.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Others like Ms Jessica Tan have raised concerns that the middle income may have been missed in the short-term support measures.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In this Budget, I have set aside a total of $42 billion for our social spending and transfers, 35% more than FY2019.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is on top of: our security spending, which ensures the safety of our people and allows property and asset prices to rise over time, in line with our economic fundamentals, our investments in the economy which ensure that our people have access to good jobs for many years to come.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And we have different schemes and components in our support packages.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Others, like the upcoming CDC Vouchers, are provided to all, including our middle class.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, we should not look at each Budget in terms of "goodies for me", but whether the totality of the spending creates more opportunities for us and our children.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I fully understand the aspirations of our middle class earners.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is natural that we want to do better for ourselves each passing year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Like Ms Janet Ang has said, the Singapore Dream is a work-in-progress.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We wish for every future generation to be better off than the last.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, let me reiterate the measures that the Government has put in place to support these.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, we have quality housing, which is affordable to all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Even in land-scarce Singapore, you can see in this chart  , our housing prices are lower than those of many major international cities, even before accounting for grants.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We provide housing subsidies to keep HDB flats affordable.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The current income ceiling of $14,000 allows eight in 10 Singaporeans to buy a subsidised HDB flat.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our homes may not be the largest or the cheapest, but we definitely have well-built, affordable housing options, in a safe, secure and green environment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Next, we have strong support for couples who want to raise a family.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Miss Cheng Li Hui and Ms Hany Soh asked for more to be done to support parenthood and first-time parents.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over the years, the Government has strengthened support for families with children, to defray the cost of education and childcare, through a combination of broad-based grants, subsidies and tax benefits.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This includes a $4,000 MediSave grant which covers the child’s MediShield Life premiums from birth till age 21.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Even more support is available for those who come from less-privileged backgrounds.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These include job opportunities, support for their jobs and livelihoods, re-designing jobs for more progressive workplaces, encouraging higher technology adoption amongst women, and support for care-giving.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These are good points which we can continue to work together.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Children also have access to an affordable education, supported by nurturing teachers, which ensures that our children are equipped with important knowledge and skills to perform to the best of their potential.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We nurture our students’ aspirations and continue to develop multiple pathways to enable our students to learn, including through industry attachments.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Third, I assure Mr Louis Chua that we remain committed to helping all seniors retire with greater peace of mind through the CPF system.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Silver Support Scheme provides support for our seniors who had low incomes during their working years and need additional support in retirement.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over the next five years, to help more Singaporeans meet the Basic Retirement Sum, we will also be providing an additional boost through the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are also in a fortunate position where most of our seniors have housing assets which they could use to support their retirement, if they choose to.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Last but not least, the Government provides good and affordable healthcare to all Singaporeans, especially our seniors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This went into expanding healthcare capacity and enhancing healthcare subsidies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We now spend more than twice the amount on patient subsidies than we did 10 years ago and expect to spend more as our population ages.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: On average, a Singaporean can expect to receive about $200,000 in Government healthcare subsidies throughout their lifetime.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As a result, we do well in terms of health outcomes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Indeed, Singapore ranks amongst the top for the World Bank’s Human Capital Index, which measures the ability of a child to reach his or her full potential if they had full health and complete, high-quality education.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We also do well in the Bloomberg Health-Efficiency Index, which measures life expectancy as compared to medical spending.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In 2019, our average life expectancy at birth was 84.9 years, with health-adjusted life expectancy of 74.5 years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Globally, Singaporeans are expected to live the longest!

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Ms Hany Soh will be glad to know that we have put in strong support for young parents.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A young couple buying a HDB flat near their parents could benefit from more than $134,000 in support in this year alone.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Besides housing grants, the support includes pre-school subsidies to help with the education of their child, healthcare subsidies, and also offsets for expenses through the Household Support Package.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Another example is a multi-generational family that already owns their 5-room HDB flat, supporting a Pioneer Generation senior with disabilities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The family could receive over $35,000 in support this year in education and healthcare subsidies, including $1,200 from the Household Support Package.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And these are over and above the housing subsidies that the family would have enjoyed when it first bought the flat.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Neither family needs to pay their MediShield Life and CareShield Life premium in cash.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: No one will lose coverage due to inability to pay.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, with the most important items in life well taken care of, I hope Members like Mr Leong Mun Wai will agree that his position that our support is, I quote, "ad hoc, short-term and unpredictable" is wrong.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In fact, our support is systematic, well-structured and balanced.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
